annotation.title_clean: Robot Teachers As A Next Step In Algorithmic Education? Ethical Considerations At The Interfaces Between Humanism, Digital Humanism And Critical Posthumanism
annotation.title_en: Robot Teachers As A Next Step In Algorithmic Education? Ethical Considerations At The Interfaces Between Humanism, Digital Humanism And Critical Posthumanism
annotation.venue: International Journal of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual journal article examining ethical issues of robots as teachers and learning companions through humanism, digital humanism and critical posthumanism. It situates them within "algorithmic education" and discusses machine moral agency, pedagogical autonomy, relational quality and distribution of responsibility, arguing for deliberate, ethical integration that augments human teachers.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines 'algorithmic education' as an umbrella for digitalization, automation, AI and platformization in education.
Questions applicability of machine moral agency and artificial morality in educational contexts.
Argues robots should augment, not replace, teachers, with educators involved in design.
Highlights responsibility, autonomy, equity and EdTech industry interests as ethical concerns.
Draws on roboethics frameworks (security, responsibility, governance, democracy, transparency, values).
